body.statement: For \(p=2\) and \((G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), the eight loading-line choices are sound and complete on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), and the finite product defining this locus, including \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\), is nonzero on every full-dimensional ambient chamber. On each branch, \(v'=v'_0+sn\), \(m_2=\zeta\ell_1+\rho_2\ell_2\), and \(g=v'_1x\ell_1+v'_2\ell_2\); for \(k\in\{3,4\}\), \(\beta_k=\det[m_k,\ell_k]/\det[g,\ell_k]\), \(m_k-\beta_kg=\rho_k\ell_k\), \(h'_k=\beta_k(x,1,0,0)\), and \(t'_k=v'_k+2\rho_k-\beta_k^2(v'_1x^2+v'_2)\), while \(h'_2=(\zeta/v'_1,0,0,0)\) and \(t'_2=v'_2+2\rho_2-\zeta^2/v'_1\). A finite bivariate sign decomposition in \((s,x)\), together with the exact support hyperplane exclusions, classifies the union over every full-dimensional true sign and variance chamber \(C\subset\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) and returns either a legal-twin cover dense relative to \(C\) or a separator with full dimension relative to \(C\), verified in the original five covariance equations. Legal twins may be variance-neutral. In addition, for each \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), there is a relatively open semialgebraic neighborhood of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\) inside its generic chamber and a legal covariance-twin branch on that neighborhood, certified by a nonzero Jacobian minor from \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\). Both signs of every true variance change are covered; no pointwise assertion is made on a true variance-neutral hyperplane.
body.justification: This is the mandatory first proved deliverable and the early kill test for whether graph-specific branch geometry can replace unrestricted real quantifier elimination.
body.gap: The closest LCD results give neither an exhaustive positive eight-branch classification nor a nonsingular open covariance collision checked against every original context equation.
body.consumer: This supplies the smallest auditable instance of the positive-real classification motivated by Problem 5.2 and the template the general compiler must reproduce.
